title: Open naturality of the diagonal pasting maps
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, of [def-pur-conventions], with the specified global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the small pro-etale constructible exceptional inverse images and derived operations of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ and let $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru^!Rv^!$ be the conjugate of compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\theta_{h,M}:Lh^*M\otimes^L\omega_h\to Rh^!M$ be the specified tensor map [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps $u,v$ define
$$\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\circ\theta_{u,\omega_v}\circ\mathrm{sym}:\omega_u\otimes^LLu^*\omega_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{vu}.$$
For $h=f,g,gf$, write $W_h=\operatorname{dom}(h)\times_{\operatorname{cod}(h)}\operatorname{dom}(h)$, $p_h$ for its first projection, $\Delta_h$ for the diagonal, $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant], and $\alpha_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ for the specified diagonal base-change map [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change].

Put $Q=X\times_ZY$, $W=X\times_ZX$, $a:W\to Q$, $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1,f(x_2))$, $b:Q\to X$, $(x,y)\mapsto x$, $t=\Delta_{gf}:X\to W$, and $s=(\operatorname{id}_X,f):X\to Q$. These formulas denote the maps induced by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $at=s$, $ba=p_{gf}$, and the Cartesian base-change maps identify $C_f\cong Lt^*\omega_a$ and $Lf^*C_g\cong Ls^*\omega_b$. Define the section-pasting comparison, using these maps and the monoidal pullback reassociation, by
$$\kappa:C_f\otimes^LLf^*C_g\xrightarrow{\sim}Lt^*(\omega_a\otimes^LLa^*\omega_b)\xrightarrow{Lt^*\sigma_{a,b}}C_{gf}.$$
Let X', Y', Z' be finite-type k-schemes and let u:X'→X, v:Y'→Y and w:Z'→Z be arbitrary open immersions. Let f':X'→Y' and g':Y'→Z' be the restricted smooth separated finite-type maps of pure dimensions d,e, so u f=f' v and v g=g' w. The squares need only commute. Define the restriction maps O_h on dualizing objects by first applying smooth base change along the target open and then the unique counit-normalized exceptional restriction along the residual source-open immersion. Define S_h on diagonal section objects by applying this construction to the two restricted factors of their self-products and pulling along their diagonals. Use canonical monoidal and composition comparisons to identify the restricted tensor domains. Then alpha_f, alpha_g and alpha_gf commute with S_f/O_f, S_g/O_g and S_gf/O_gf respectively; sigma_f,g commutes with the tensor restriction O_f tensor f'^*O_g and O_gf; kappa_f,g commutes with the tensor restriction S_f tensor f'^*S_g and S_gf; gamma_f commutes with S_f and the section-pullback restriction of omega_a; and gamma_g commutes with the restriction of f^*C_g and that of s^*omega_b. Equality means equality after the canonical comparison inverse image to the small pro-etale derived category. These are exactly the seven squares of OpenEquation, with no global pasting or affine coordinate assertion. Source-open squares are not assumed Cartesian. This includes empty open schemes and d=0 or e=0. Use the canonical normalization of the constructed comparisons from [def-pur-diagonal-section-pasting-data].

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-dualizing-sigma-cocycle-locality] to the expressions for $\gamma_f,\gamma_g$ and $\kappa$. Target-open restrictions are Cartesian base changes; source-open restrictions use its normalized etale $E$ and its displayed compatibility with $\beta$. The diagonal factors through the open pair obtained by restricting both factors. Pulling these expressions along that diagonal therefore gives their specified comparisons for every compatible source and target restriction, including the equality from Step 1.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonalSectionPastingOpen (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    {X Y Z X' Y' Z' : Scheme.{u}}
    (d e : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (g' : Y' ⟶ Z')
    (u' : X' ⟶ X) (v : Y' ⟶ Y) (w : Z' ⟶ Z)
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian Z]
    [IsNoetherian X'] [IsNoetherian Y'] [IsNoetherian Z']
    [IsOpenImmersion u'] [IsOpenImmersion v] [IsOpenImmersion w]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e g]
    [IsSeparated f'] [LocallyOfFiniteType f'] [QuasiCompact f']
    [IsSeparated g'] [LocallyOfFiniteType g'] [QuasiCompact g']
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f'] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e g']
    (hf : u' ≫ f = f' ≫ v) (hg : v ≫ g = g' ≫ w)
    (aZ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aZ] [QuasiCompact aZ] :
    letI := P.comparedExponent (𝟙 (Spec (.of P.field.k)))
    OpenEquation P.Coefficient P d e f g f' g' u' v w hf hg aZ
